summary: A single 700px column in Chicago-flag colours on charcoal: hero, download and credits lines, a one-block style and character sheet, then Carl Sandburg's whole poem 'Chicago', from which the family takes its name, set line by line with every line fitted to the column width. The poem is the specimen; there is no script-driven interaction beyond the fit-to-width.

instances.look: 'BIG' plus four red Chicago-flag stars, 'SHOULDERS' below, and 'is a suite of typefaces for Chicagoans', each line fitted to the 700px column in sky blue and white on charcoal
instances.learn: Use the four stars of the local flag as a typed glyph in the wordmark: place identity costs one line of text and no image

reconstruction.layout: Centred 700px column from y=8; three stacked lines, each scaled to the full column width, ~420px tall, negative margins between lines (-40px, -20px). Blue horizontal bar 750×60px follows
reconstruction.typography: 'BIG✶✶✶✶' ~147px ExtraBold uppercase; 'SHOULDERS' ~165px ExtraBold uppercase; tagline ~57px Regular sentence case white. Stars are text, red
reconstruction.behaviour: SlabText.js fits each span to the column on load and on resize, setting font-size and microscopic word and letter spacing inline
reconstruction.html: p.slabtextdone > span.slabtext.bsxb.big.blue > span.red for the stars

instances.look: Sandburg's full poem in the column: 'CHICAGO' at 220px in blue, then stanza after stanza of lines fitted to 700px in shifting weights and small caps, the size set by line length, with BAREHEADED, / SHOVELING, / WRECKING… running Thin to Black and a red 'Laughing!' at 212px
instances.ux: Static; a plain scroll, the page rhythm comes from the changing line sizes
instances.learn: A public-domain text with a rhythm of its own does the art direction: fitting every line to the measure and mapping weight to the words gives you a whole-page poster for free
